facts.text: I have one table named t1 with columns code and punchdatetime.
The table t1 does not identify whether punchdatetime is an in punch or an out punch.
I have another table named t2 with columns code, calendardate, start time, and end time.
The table t2 has each date shift start and end datetime in start time and endtime columns for that date.
For weekly offs in t2, the start time and end time are null.
If punches are available for a working day or weekly off, I want to pair the punches and show details including code, calendardate, start datetime, end datetime, punching, and punchout.
Punches can be picked before 4 hours of the start time and after 4 hours of the end time.
For weekly off, the previous day endtime after 4 hours should be paired to the next-day.
If punches are not available in t1, I want the result to display as null.
Or conditions in my SQL query are taking time and giving many records, and the data is not correct.
If punchnot is not available, it should return null.
Punchdatetime should exist in t1, otherwise the employee may have forgotten to punch.
If a record does not exist in t1, I want it to show null.

keyphrases: t2 table code calendardate start time endtime
weekly off start time end time null
4 hours window before start and after end
check for nulls instead of OR
